finalExcerpt:
I fixed `parse_price` in `inventory.py`, and all 5 tests pass, including the new regression test.

`parse_price` now treats commas as thousands separators when the string is comma groups of exactly three digits and either has a decimal point (`"1,234.50"` → `1234.5`) or has more than one comma (`"$1,234,567"` → `1234567.0`). Everything else keeps the old behavior, so `"12.50"`, `"$3"` and `"12,50"` → `12.5` still work. I didn't touch `total_value`.

A lone `"1,234"` with no dot is still read as a European decimal (`1.234`). The issue only calls a comma a thousands separator when a dot or another comma group follows, so I left that case alone.

The regression test, `test_thousands_separator`, is in `tests/test_inventory.py`.
